name: Ringo Corponation Fractal Handshake Coin
description:
The Fractal Handshake Coin is a physical cryptographic authentication and one-time-use secure channel initiator disguised as an unremarkable commemorative coin — the kind sold in tourist traps and corporate lobbies across Meridian 88. Embedded within the coin's interior is a fractal key generator chip, a compressed burst transmitter, and a self-destruct thermite micro-charge. When the coin is handled in a specific way — a particular sequence of pressure points applied to obverse and reverse faces — it initiates a one-time cryptographic handshake with a designated receiver, establishing a temporary, fully authenticated, end-to-end encrypted communication channel that exists for a maximum of ninety seconds before the coin destroys its own key material and becomes inert.

The channel established by the Coin is authenticated against a fractal key tree that makes replay attacks and man-in-the-middle interception mathematically intractable within the channel's operational window. No persistent infrastructure is required — the coin carries everything needed to bootstrap the secure channel from scratch. The receiver endpoint can be a hardware terminal, a compatible implant, or another Coin held by a paired party. After use, the coin is physically identical to any other commemorative coin and passes all standard contraband scans.

Ringo Corponation markets the Fractal Handshake Coin as a 'legacy authentication solution' for high-value executive communications, but its real market is anyone who needs to establish a provably secure channel with no pre-existing digital relationship and no persistent infrastructure — a one-time meeting between parties who have never communicated before and may never do so again.

cultural_context: The Fractal Handshake Coin has taken on a cultural weight in Meridian 88's criminal and intelligence ecosystems disproportionate to its technical specifications. Being handed a Coin is understood as an act of significant trust — it means someone is willing to spend a one-time-use, difficult-to-obtain authentication device to speak with you. Conversely, receiving a Coin from an unknown party is treated with extreme caution, as it implies someone wants a provably deniable first contact. Ringo's choice to disguise them as commemorative coins means they move freely through the city, carried in pockets and on keychains without raising flags.

story_hooks: A dead fixer's belongings include seventeen unused Fractal Handshake Coins — far more than any single operator should carry. Someone was either preparing for a massive operation or stockpiling them as currency.

The players receive a Coin from an anonymous source with no explanation; activating it connects them to someone who claims to have information that will get them all killed if they don't act within the hour.

A Ringo Corponation employee is leaking the fractal key tree master tables that allow all issued Coins to be decrypted retroactively — every channel ever opened with a Ringo Coin is about to become readable.

The players are hired to recover a specific Coin before its intended recipient uses it; whoever activated it first gets the channel, and the wrong party activating it could compromise an entire network of informants.
